title: COP31 climate talks end with no deal after fossil fuels row derails hopes of agreement
html:
Image source, Reuters

Fossil fuels were formed from the remains of dead organisms over millions of years. They are non-renewable resources - meaning once we've used them, they run out.

Much of the world’s energy is produced by burning fossil fuels such as oil, coal and gas - which are used to power everything from cars, planes, gas cookers and heating in homes.

But burning these fuels creates carbon dioxide gas (CO2), which traps extra energy in the atmosphere near the Earth's surface and causes the planet to be warmer than it should be, adding to climate change.

Fossil fuels are by far the largest driver of global climate change.
summary: Several countries and the EU rejected the deal over its failure to refer to the need to phase out fossil fuels.
